ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy set with monster Other One jam and tight Truckin' sequence
ai_show_review.blurb: The Salt Palace show bursts with nonstop momentum, highlighted by a soaring China Cat > I Know You Rider segue and an epic Truckin'/The Other One/Eyes of the World/Morning Dew stretch. Jerry’s vocals are in prime form and Phil’s bass drives the extended jams. The recording captures a classic early‑’73 performance that rewards any Deadhead.
ai_show_review.review: February 28, 1973 at Salt Palace finds the Dead firing on all cylinders. From the opening Cold Rain And Snow through a punchy Jack Straw, the first set builds solidly and hands off to a second set that flows like a single, uninterrupted groove. China Cat Sunflower slides seamlessly into I Know You Rider before launching into a monster The Other One that erupts into one of the most memorable Truckin' > The Other One > Eyes of the World > Morning Dew passages of the era. Jerry’s vocal delivery is crisp and his guitar solos—especially on Cold Rain And Snow and the Truckin' jam—are nothing short of dazzling. Phil’s “blow‑torch” bass underpins every improvisational turn, while Keith’s piano adds a lush, supportive texture throughout. Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming stays tight yet propulsive, giving the band room to explore without losing focus. Donna Jean’s harmonies lift Row Jimmy and He’s Gone, rounding out a performance that captures the restless creativity of early‑’70s Dead at their peak.

best_recording.reason: Good soundboard source with clear, balanced mix and minimal cuts; captures the monster Other One jam and tight Truckin'/Eyes sequence without the early muffling found in other versions.

key_highlights: Monster The Other One jam that builds into a soaring improvisational peak
Seamless China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider transition launching the second set
Extended Truckin' > The Other One > Eyes of the World > Morning Dew sequence showcases tight group interplay

band_performance.Jerry: Vocals are excellent and his guitar work shines, especially a flawless solo on Cold Rain And Snow and an explosive blues‑scale burst during the Truckin' jam.
band_performance.Phil: Powerful bass that ‘blow‑torches’ Jack Straw and drives every extended improvisation; vocal contributions are strong as well.
band_performance.Bob: Solid rhythm guitar foundation and tight harmonies, notably on Row Jimmy where his vocals blend with Donna Jean’s.
band_performance.Keith: Piano work is near perfect, adding melodic depth to El Paso and supporting the jams without overpowering the mix.
band_performance.Billy: Tight, energetic drumming that anchors the monster Other One and keeps the extended Truckin'/Eyes flow grounded.
